title: Portable Atlas bundle (v1)
description: The public, versioned portable Atlas bundle: a self-contained migration package layered ON TOP of the landscape export (landscape.schema.json). It carries the resolved landscape plus the additional Atlas-domain metadata a hosted <-> self-hosted move needs — workspace metadata, diagrams, an attachment manifest, public module/extension data and restore hints — without becoming a private hosted-only escape hatch. It carries Atlas domain data and migration metadata only: NEVER entitlement/subscription/billing state, live identity credentials or raw secret values (those are Fabric/control-plane concerns or are represented as references/rebind instructions). See handbook 11 §3, 11 §7, 12 §Phase C and ADR 0003.

contractVersion.description: The atlas-contracts schema major version this bundle conforms to.

kind.description: Discriminates a portable bundle from the import/export/discovery documents.

createdAt.description: When the bundle was produced, if known.

generator.description: Optional provenance: what produced this bundle.

compatibility.description: Producer-declared compatibility so a reader can decide, before importing, whether it can safely consume the bundle.

manifest.description: Machine-checkable inventory of what the bundle carries, so a reader can verify completeness before importing. The counts must match the actual section sizes — a bundle-level rule the conformance kit checks.

landscape.description: The resolved landscape core: assets and manual relationships, exactly as the export contract defines them. Every reference elsewhere in the bundle points at ids in here.

workspace.description: Held, portable workspace metadata (display identity only — never tenant shell, subscription or entitlement state).

diagrams.description: Portable Atlas diagrams: held layouts over the landscape, referencing asset and relationship ids present in it.

attachments.description: Attachment MANIFEST: references to binary attachments with integrity digests, never inline secret bytes. The bytes themselves travel out of band; this lists what belongs to the bundle and how to verify it.

modules.description: Public module / extension data sections. Each carries a public module id and the version of that module's OWN public data contract; the payload is governed by that module contract, not this one.

restore.description: Restore HINTS for reconstructing the workspace at the destination: identity-mapping placeholders and secret-rebind instructions. Instructions and references only — never password/session material or secret values.

excluded.description: The non-portable categories the producer asserts it deliberately left out. Makes the exclusions machine-visible so a reader knows the bundle is complete-by-design, not truncated. The schema also structurally forbids carrying these (additionalProperties: false everywhere).

BundleCompatibility.description: Producer-declared compatibility floor and provenance. Additive changes keep a bundle readable by older readers within the same contract major; breaking changes raise the contract major (schemas/v2) with an ADR and migration.

minReaderContractVersion.description: The minimum atlas-contracts schema major version a reader must implement to safely import this bundle. For v1 this is '1'; a reader on an older major must refuse rather than silently drop data.

producerAtlasVersion.description: The version of the Atlas runtime that produced the bundle, if known. A hint for the destination, not a gate.

requiredModules.description: Public module ids (and minimum versions) the destination must have available to fully restore the module sections. A reader missing one can still import the landscape core.

ModuleRequirement.description: A public module the destination should have to consume a module data section.

minVersion.description: The minimum public data-contract version of the module the destination needs.

BundleManifest.description: Inventory of the bundle's sections. Counts must equal the actual array sizes; the SDK exposes the check and the conformance kit enforces it.

landscape.description: Counts for the embedded landscape core.

WorkspaceMetadata.description: Portable workspace display metadata. Cataloguing/presentation only: NO tenant shell, subscription, entitlement, trial or billing state (Fabric/control-plane, recreated or remapped at the destination).

slug.description: A stable, URL-safe short name, if the workspace has one.

locale.description: Preferred display locale (BCP-47 tag, e.g. 'da-DK'). Presentation preference, not policy.

timeZone.description: Preferred display time zone (IANA tz id, e.g. 'Europe/Copenhagen').

Diagram.description: A portable diagram: a held visual layout over the landscape. Node placements reference asset ids and edges reference relationship ids that MUST be present in the embedded landscape (a bundle-level rule the conformance kit checks). A rendered image, if any, is carried as an attachment, not inline.

id.description: Stable diagram identifier, unique within the bundle.

format.description: The layout format. 'atlas-layout' is the held node/edge placement below; other public formats may be added additively.

nodes.description: Placed assets. Each 'ref' matches an asset 'id' in the embedded landscape.

edges.description: Drawn relationships. Each 'ref' matches a relationship 'id' in the embedded landscape.

renderRef.description: Optional attachment id (an entry in 'attachments') of a rendered image of this diagram.

DiagramNode.description: A placed asset in a diagram. Position is a held layout fact, not analysis.

ref.description: The asset id this node draws, present in the embedded landscape.

DiagramEdge.description: A drawn relationship in a diagram.

ref.description: The relationship id this edge draws, present in the embedded landscape.

AttachmentManifestEntry.description: One attachment listed by reference and integrity digest — never inline secret bytes. The bytes travel out of band (an external store, or a sidecar in the transport container); this entry lets the destination locate and verify them.

id.description: Stable attachment identifier, unique within the bundle. Referenced by diagrams' 'renderRef' and by 'attachedToRef'.

byteSize.description: Size of the attachment in bytes.

digest.description: Content digest so the destination can verify the out-of-band bytes.

attachedToRef.description: Optional id of the asset, relationship or diagram this attachment belongs to. When set, it must resolve within the bundle.

Digest.description: A content digest. SHA-256 is the required baseline; other algorithms may be added additively.

ModuleData.description: A public module / extension data section. The bundle contract fixes only the envelope (which module, which of ITS contract versions); the payload shape is governed by that module's own public contract and is therefore opaque here. A module must never use this section to smuggle secrets or entitlement state — the same exclusions apply.

version.description: The version of the module's OWN public data contract that governs 'data'.

itemCount.description: Optional count of items in 'data', for manifest-style verification by the module's reader.

data.description: The module's portable payload, governed by the module's own public contract (referenced by 'id'+'version'). Opaque to this contract.

ModuleId.description: A public module / extension identifier, e.g. 'atlas.diagramming' or a third-party reverse-DNS id.

RestoreHints.description: Non-data instructions for reconstructing the workspace at the destination. Placeholders and instructions only: identity is rebound to the destination IdP, and secrets are rebound at the destination — this section NEVER carries password/session material or secret values.

identityMappings.description: Placeholders mapping a source principal reference to a destination-binding hint. No credentials — the destination binds identities to its own IdP.

secretRebinds.description: Instructions for rebinding a secret at the destination, keyed by an opaque reference. No secret values.

notes.description: Free-text operator notes for the restore.

IdentityMapping.description: One identity-mapping placeholder. Carries references and hints, never credentials.

sourceRef.description: An opaque reference to the source principal (e.g. a stable user key). Not an email, not a credential.

displayName.description: Optional display name to help an operator match the principal at the destination.

bindHint.description: Optional hint for binding at the destination (e.g. 'match by corporate directory group X').

SecretRebind.description: One secret-rebind instruction. Names WHAT must be re-provided at the destination, never the value.

ref.description: An opaque reference to the secret in the source (e.g. a key-vault path or logical name). Not the secret itself.

instruction.description: How to re-provide the secret at the destination.

ExcludedCategory.description: A category of state that is deliberately NOT portable through the bundle.
